lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: problems with models, equations, and checks
lessonRef.title: Performance task: build: problems with models, equations, and checks

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A store arranges 7 shelves with 4 boxes on each shelf, then adds 9 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
The pattern 7, 11, 15, 19, ... continues by the same rule. What is the 5th term?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A store arranges 7 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then adds 6 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
The pattern 6, 9, 12, 15, ... continues by the same rule. What is the 7th term?
A store arranges 6 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then adds 8 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
The pattern 1, 9, 17, 25, ... continues by the same rule. What is the 5th term?
A store arranges 5 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then sells 11 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and say how you would check it is right.

items.prompt: The pattern 1, 6, 11, 16, ... continues by the same rule. What is the 5th term?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A store arranges 7 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then adds 19 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
